parts:
n 8/24/12 12:23 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> I stand by what I said, but ... there's a bunch of mentions of boost_1.50.0 and eigen_3.1.0 in the reference manual that
> are going to be annoying to change.

Right -- I was originally hoping to just have a
higher-level lib so as not to have to mention
versions. But that shortcut was a bad idea.

I very much like them versions in the source
distribution. I like to easily see what I'm getting
when I download a package.
> Is there some way to run a script from inside a .tex file to get those?

Sure, I can run find-and-replace over directories.
That's how I changed the models to the new syntax.
And these long unique names are easy targets.

> Or can we
> just make lib/boost and lib/eigen symlinks to whatever is the latest version of the libraries we are shipping without
> breaking on Windows?

I don't know about symlinks, but I was hoping to
encapsulate everything behind make.

The make scripts are now pretty impenetrable, but
it's easy to follow what they do. So I'll probably
show some output from make running to indicate that,
and note that it might be out of date version-wise
from the current Stan.

- Bob

PS g++ barfed on Boost 1.51. Another problem with
mdivide_left_tri, that we already had a workaround
for, mdivide_left_tri_low. So I'll push that fix with
the lib update I'm about to run.

I don't know what g++'s problem is with these templates.
They look fine to everyone who's looked at them and they
work fine in clang++. And that specific call worked in
the previous g++.

messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Boost 1.51 (& g++ issues with templates)
parts:
It might be useful to include a template Makefile for building models in the documentation. Then the instructions are simply (1) copy the makefile  the directory with the Stan model, (2) edit some variables at the top of the makefile, and (3) run make. I know the first time I tried compiling a model, I ended up having to look through the makefile to get it to work.  Below, I pasted what I am currently using as a Makefile. 

Regarding the Boost/Eigen versions in the LaTeX, you can define a macro with the current version that is being used \newcommand{\BoostVer}{1.51} and then use that macro for all the mentions in the documentation.

# Directory of models
SRC_DIR = .
# Output directory 
OUT_DIR = ./ 
# Location of stan
STAN_HOME = $(HOME)/remotes/stan
# Extension name for compiled objects
EXE = .stanx

# Compiler to use
CC = g++
# Level of optimization
O = 3

# DO NOT EDIT below that line
###################################################################################

# Create objects
source = $(wildcard $(SRC_DIR)/*.stan)
# TODO: slash direction would need to be generalized for cross-platform.
objects = $(addprefix $(OUT_DIR)/,$(notdir $(patsubst %.stan,%$(EXE),$(source))))

# TODO: insert OS specific stuff
AR = ar

# Stan Paths
STAN_BIN = $(STAN_HOME)/bin/
STAN_SRC = $(STAN_HOME)/src/
STAN_LIB = $(STAN_HOME)/lib/
STANC = $(STAN_BIN)/stanc

# Library locations
# Kind of robust to version changes 
# and multiple versions (taking one, and usually the last one)
EIGEN ?= $(lastword $(sort $(wildcard $(STAN_LIB)/eigen_*)))
BOOST ?= $(lastword $(sort $(wildcard $(STAN_LIB)/boost_*)))

##
# Set default compiler options.
## 
CFLAGS = -I $(STAN_SRC) -I $(EIGEN) -I $(EIGEN)/unsupported -I $(BOOST) -O$O -fPIC
LDLIBS = -L$(STAN_BIN) -lstan
LDLIBS_STANC = -L$(STAN_BIN) -lstanc

%.cpp : %.stan 
@echo ''
@echo '--- Translating Stan graphical model to C++ code ---'
$(STANC) --name=$(basename $(notdir $<)) --o=$@ $<  

%.o : %.cpp
@echo ''
@echo '--- Compiling C++ code ---'
$(COMPILE.c) $(OUTPUT_OPTION) $<

%$(EXE) : %.o
@echo ''
@echo '--- Linking C++ model ---'
$(LINK.c) $(OUTPUT_OPTION) $< $(LDLIBS)

all: $(objects)

.SECONDARY:

clean:
-rm -f $(MODEL_DIR)/*.cpp $(MODEL_DIR)/*.$(EXE) $(MODEL_DIR)/*.o

On 8/24/12 12:02 PM, Jeffrey Arnold wrote:
> It might be useful to include a template Makefile for building models in the documentation. Then the instructions are
> simply (1) copy the makefile the directory with the Stan model, (2) edit some variables at the top of the makefile, and
> (3) run make. I know the first time I tried compiling a model, I ended up having to look through the makefile to get it
> to work. Below, I pasted what I am currently using as a Makefile.

I hope to get around to doing the command-line
getting started.

You don't need to do (1) or (2). You can just
call

> make <makefile path> -D<key>=<value> ...

with a path to the makefile and the -D option to
override any of the options.

> Regarding the Boost/Eigen versions in the LaTeX, you can define a macro with the current version that is being used
> \newcommand{\BoostVer}{1.51} and then use that macro for all the mentions in the documentation.

That might work other than for refs in Verbatim
mode (and it might even work there as I'm using
the package and it gives you various options).

- Bob
